note: Which behavioural concern each front door is expected to unit-test, and every accepted gap with its reason. Read by tools/tests/test_coverage_parity.py. Three implementations of one detector should be tested to the same depth; where they are not, the divergence is declared here with a reason rather than discovered by counting test files a year later. Adding a suite to one port and not the others fails this file, and so does adding one this file does not declare — the check runs in both directions, because a suite nothing declares is how a concern ends up tested in one port only.

primitives.why: The shared primitives spec, one test per case family plus the constant tables.

candidates.why: Candidate generation internals — the regexes, the capitalisation habit, the relation window, the corroboration guard. Distinct from `primitives`: that checks agreement with the reference on recorded cases, this names each behaviour so a failure says which rule broke rather than which case differs.

structured.why: The structured-identifier pass — phone, email, SSN, card with its Luhn gate, address, ZIP, age, DOB, username, URL — and the order they are applied in.

redact.why: The public entry point: identity interpolation, the two passes, arm selection, and the restore map.

gazetteer.why: The notability index as the detector reads it: the fold, tier precedence, the title prefix walk, and the demonym tier's KEEP.

lexicon.why: The stoplist and the shipped word lists as loaded from the asset.

asset.why: Loading the vendored asset, verifying its digest, and refusing one that declares an unknown tier.

conformance.why: Reading the shared spec and scoring the 54 frames off the file.

gates.why: The nine gates, the NOT MEASURED discipline, and each port's own bars against the published ones.

packaging.why: That the built artifact carries the asset and installs, and that the release path's own logic — the conformance gate, the pack-contents reader, the is-it-really-published check — is exercised without cutting a release. A packaging break is invisible to every other suite and shows up for whoever runs install first.

regex_dialect.why: Where this language's regex dialect disagrees with Python's, asserted in BOTH directions: the pattern as written gives the reference answer, and the idiomatic local spelling gives a different one. Ruby anchors `^`/`$` per line; JavaScript's `\b`, `\w` and `\d` are ASCII-only and its `$` does not match before a trailing newline. Renamed from `dialect` on 2026-08-12: that name and its description claimed the concern was demonyms, which is not what either suite tests, and no check could see the mismatch because the description is prose.

config.why: Environment-variable resolution: which name wins, what counts as unset, and the legacy-name fallbacks.

local_classifier.why: The local PII classifier the reference's recall harness measures — its false-positive guards and its honest boundary at third-party names.

accepted_divergences.reason: JUSTIFIED. Python's gazetteer tests are about BUILDING the asset and moved to tools/tests/test_gazetteer_build.py; the runtime read path is covered by tests/test_assets.py and by the primitives spec. The other two ports only ever read the asset, so a read-path suite is the whole of their concern.
JUSTIFIED. Python generates the stoplist rather than loading it, so the equivalent assertions live in the tools suite beside the generator.
JUSTIFIED. Python IS the reference, so 'does this port match the spec' is instead 'does the spec still match this port', which is tools/tests/test_conformance.py.

JUSTIFIED. Python is the dialect the other two are measured against, so there is no divergence for it to pin — the question 'does this port's regex engine agree with the reference' is not askable of the reference. Its build-time demonym derivation, which the old `dialect` description wrongly folded in here, is tools/tests/test_demonyms_and_carryover.py.

JUSTIFIED. There is no local_classifier module in this port and none is planned. It belongs to the reference's evaluation harness — the thing that MEASURES recall against injected ground truth — not to the detector the three front doors implement. A port of it would be a second detector to keep in parity for no caller's benefit.

JUSTIFIED. Same as TypeScript: the module is the reference evaluation harness's, not the detector's. Recorded rather than left undeclared, which is how it sat until 2026-08-12 — 41 collected Python tests belonging to no declared concern, invisible to this file because nothing checked the on-disk-to-declared direction.
